title: Calculate Physician Patient Workload
description_markdown: Clinical request: For each doctor in `doctors`, count completed patient appointments as `completed_visits`. Return `d.name`, `d.specialization`, and `completed_visits`. Order by `completed_visits` DESC, `d.doctor_id` ASC.
starter_query:
-- Doctor visit count
SELECT ...
solution_query: SELECT d.name, d.specialization, COUNT(a.appointment_id) AS completed_visits FROM doctors d LEFT JOIN appointments a ON d.doctor_id = a.doctor_id AND a.status = 'completed' GROUP BY d.doctor_id, d.name, d.specialization ORDER BY completed_visits DESC, d.doctor_id ASC;
solution_explanation: Counts completed appointments per doctor while keeping doctors with 0 appointments via LEFT JOIN.
hints: Include condition in LEFT JOIN: `AND a.status = 'completed'`.
Focus on the required WHERE, JOIN, or GROUP BY clause conditions.

Query: SELECT d.name, d.specialization, COUNT(a.appointment_id) AS completed_visits FROM doctors d LEFT JOIN appointments a ON d.doctor_id = a.doctor_id AND a.status = 'completed' GROUP BY d.doctor_id, d.name, d.specialization ORDER BY completed_visits DESC, d.doctor_id ASC;

title: Identify Recurring Patients with Multiple Appointments
description_markdown: Care coordination request: Find patients who have had strictly more than 1 appointment. Return `p.patient_id`, `p.name`, `p.blood_group`, and `COUNT(a.appointment_id) AS visit_count`. Order by `visit_count` DESC, `p.patient_id` ASC.
starter_query:
-- Patients with > 1 visits
SELECT ...
solution_query: SELECT p.patient_id, p.name, p.blood_group, COUNT(a.appointment_id) AS visit_count FROM patients p JOIN appointments a ON p.patient_id = a.patient_id GROUP BY p.patient_id, p.name, p.blood_group HAVING COUNT(a.appointment_id) > 1 ORDER BY visit_count DESC, p.patient_id ASC;
solution_explanation: Identifies recurring outpatient visits using HAVING.
hints: Use `HAVING COUNT(a.appointment_id) > 1`.
Focus on the required WHERE, JOIN, or GROUP BY clause conditions.

Query: SELECT p.patient_id, p.name, p.blood_group, COUNT(a.appointment_id) AS visit_count FROM patients p JOIN appointments a ON p.patient_id = a.patient_id GROUP BY p.patient_id, p.name, p.blood_group HAVING COUNT(a.appointment_id) > 1 ORDER BY visit_count DESC, p.patient_id ASC;

title: Prescription Regimen Days by Department
description_markdown: Pharmacy request: Join `prescriptions`, `appointments`, and `doctors`. For each doctor department, calculate the total number of prescriptions issued (`COUNT(pr.prescription_id)` as `total_prescriptions`), and average duration in days (`ROUND(AVG(pr.duration_days), 1)` as `avg_days`). Return `d.department`, `total_prescriptions`, and `avg_days`. Order by `total_prescriptions` DESC, `d.department` ASC.
starter_query:
-- Prescription duration aggregates
SELECT ...
solution_query: SELECT d.department, COUNT(pr.prescription_id) AS total_prescriptions, ROUND(AVG(pr.duration_days), 1) AS avg_days FROM doctors d JOIN appointments a ON d.doctor_id = a.doctor_id JOIN prescriptions pr ON a.appointment_id = pr.appointment_id GROUP BY d.department ORDER BY total_prescriptions DESC, d.department ASC;
solution_explanation: Aggregates medication durations across clinical specialties.
hints: Join doctors -> appointments -> prescriptions.
Focus on the required WHERE, JOIN, or GROUP BY clause conditions.

Query: SELECT d.department, COUNT(pr.prescription_id) AS total_prescriptions, ROUND(AVG(pr.duration_days), 1) AS avg_days FROM doctors d JOIN appointments a ON d.doctor_id = a.doctor_id JOIN prescriptions pr ON a.appointment_id = pr.appointment_id GROUP BY d.department ORDER BY total_prescriptions DESC, d.department ASC;
